claims.statement: harnessed is a host-native Python CLI that composes catalog content (recipes into stacks) and launches the result by driving a container runtime directly from the host — podman preferred, docker supported under the id-mapping constraints of #456/#457 — with no tool container and no daemon socket; assembly runs in-process on the host and the only code that talks to a container runtime is the launch/build path (launcher.py plus the modules it drives: volumes.py, svcstate.py, ctrquery.py, credmounts.py, capability.py's live-introspection half).

The vocabulary is precise and not interchangeable: an agent is an AI coding harness defined in catalog/agents/<name>/agent.yaml (not a recipe); a recipe is a composable capability bundle added onto an agent; a service is a sidecar with its own image and service.yaml (scope global = one shared host-published container on a static port; scope project = one container per project reached through a unix socket in its data dir); a stack is a harness-free named set of recipes that may extend another; the catalog is the collection of all four.

Recipes are harness-independent: they carry no harnesses field, any harness-specific step branches on the ${HARNESS} build arg inside the recipe's Dockerfile, and every harness consumes the same committed Claude-canonical profile (HARNESS_CONFIG_DIR maps all five harnesses to .claude).

The harness is a required run-time argument on both run verbs, never a stack property, and a stack may not be named after a harness; the stack is selected by --stack/-s (mutually exclusive with repeatable --recipe/-r), giving neither runs the --extends baseline `default` as-is, and --no-extends requires at least one --recipe.

The catalog is searched across three roots in precedence order — the user overlay ~/.config/harnessed/catalog (wins on a name clash), the shipped catalog/ at harnessed_home, and last the generated root $XDG_DATA_HOME/harnessed/generated for machine-minted --recipe stacks, included only when it exists so a generated stack can never shadow an authored one.

Generated profiles are emitted to $XDG_DATA_HOME/harnessed/profiles/<stack>/<harness>/ — per-harness so the same stack's claude and omp builds never clobber each other — and never into the repo or the installed package, which stays immutable source; paths.py is the single source of truth for this and every other derived path.

src/harnessed/catalog is a symlink to the repo-root catalog/ that setuptools materializes as real files inside the wheel, so an installed harnessed carries its own agents, recipes, services, stacks, and base Dockerfiles and needs no repo on disk; paths.harnessed_home() resolves through it to a real directory containing catalog/ (repo root in a checkout, site-packages/harnessed in a wheel), honors $HARNESSED_DIR, and never derives home from the CWD — and the symlink must not be deleted or host-local links parked inside catalog/ because setuptools follows symlinks.

Every harnessed image build uses a staged temp build context (a copy of catalog/ plus the resolved extra-tools) rather than building straight from harnessed_home, so an installed wheel never gets written into and the context never ships the whole repo; catalog/ sits at the context root so the Dockerfiles' context-relative COPY paths are identical either way.

There are exactly two launch verbs, one per backend: container-run runs the stack in a container (a podman pod — isolating filesystem, network, and configuration — or a flat, self-owned-netns container on pod-less docker), ending in os.execvp into `<runtime> exec -it`, and host-run runs it host-native with no container runtime call and no MCP hub (isolating configuration only, via a per-stack CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, ending in os.execvpe of the harness); they share one stack-resolution path, and beyond the shared grammar their only shared flags are --rm and --fresh — fresh being a shared spelling with different behavior (pod teardown versus discarding the host build stamp, #452) — and both end by replacing the launcher process so the agent owns the terminal.

The execution-backend seam is harnessed.backend.ExecutionBackend: six capabilities (materialize config / provision tools / wire MCP / seed auth / wire services / apply isolation) with provision_tools and apply_isolation deliberately two-phase (FIRST_START/ATTACH and BOUNDARY/EGRESS), plus the backend-independent LaunchSpec and a name-keyed registry (@register/get_backend); there is deliberately no shared driver — sequencing is backend-owned because the two implementations do not agree on an order and cannot be made to without changing behavior.

Both conforming backend implementations live inside launcher.py beside the private helpers they call — HostBackend (name=host, isolation=none, sequenced by _launch_host) and ContainerBackend (name=container, isolation=container, sequenced by container_run) — so the dependency points into backend.py and never back out; backend-specific state (pod/instance names, volumes, mount args, host home) lives on the backend instance, never on LaunchSpec.

The two backends' capability order is deliberately asymmetric and load-bearing: the host backend materializes the per-stack home before provisioning because materializing rmtree's the very directory installs write into (holding the home lock across materialize + seed_auth + FIRST_START, and running ATTACH setups outside the lock since they may prompt), while the container backend provisions the named volumes before materializing because podman's copy-up is what lifts the image's ~/.claude into the volume the mount set then delivers.

harnessed.capmatrix is the machine-checked record of which recipe primitive each backend honors: conformance tests iterate PRIMITIVES x MATRIX so every primitive has a cell in every registered backend's column and a new backend must fill its column deliberately; exactly one cell is DEGRADED today (egress: on the host backend, whose isolation is none), and capmatrix imports nothing from launcher.py.

A services: entry is a property of the stack, not of the backend: the host backend starts the same service sidecars the container backend ensures, so a host-native launch still stands up the stack's declared services (and does so before recipe env and setup scripts so the socket exists before anything references it).

There are two console entrypoints: `harnessed` is launcher.py's Typer app (main splits argv at the first standalone -- before Typer parses so the tail reaches the harness command, and catches the persist gate's three exception types so a refusal prints as a one-line remediation), and `harnessed-tools` is cli.py's argparse entrypoint whose assemble subcommand is a standalone emit-only path usable on a machine with no container runtime.

schema.py, synclinks.py, emit.py, assemble.py, and staleness.py form the emit-only assembly chain: schema parses and validates manifests into typed objects (unknown fields preserved on .raw), synclinks fans recipes' skills/commands/rules into .claude/ failing fast on name collisions, emit writes the profile artifacts (.mcp.json, settings floor, hatago.config.json, derived Dockerfile), assemble orchestrates and runs the fail-fast authoring gates plus the recipe-closure hash, and staleness owns the .build-stamp — none of the five invokes podman/docker or touches a daemon socket.

The shared-support layer exists so extracted modules need not import launcher.py: paths.py is the single source of truth for derived paths, instance names (harnessed-<harness>-<stack>-<project_hash>), USERNS_ARG (keep-id pinned to the image's uid/gid 1000), and — since #456/#459 — runtime detection itself (active_runtime/_detect_runtime: the CONTAINER_RUNTIME override is refused unless podman or docker, podman is preferred on PATH, and ctrquery._runtime delegates rather than scanning again); layout.py holds pre-launch derivations (image tags, profile dir); proc.py supplies the three subprocess shapes including _bounded with per-command-class runtime deadlines; console.py owns the two process-wide warning-counting Consoles — a single warning counter read just before the terminal handoff — plus exec mode (set_exec_mode/in_exec_mode) and _can_prompt; ctrquery.py is the read-only runtime-predicate layer that never mutates anything.

The dependency-direction invariant: modules extracted from launcher.py import INTO the contract and into shared support and never import launcher.py, enforced by the module-boundary tests and asserted in the extracted modules' docstrings; launcher.py is a facade that re-exports the moved names because the test suite binds to them by attribute — so a new helper goes beside its callers or below them, never above, and a helper two non-launcher modules share belongs in a support module both can import.

harnessed build <stack> <harness> calls the same in-process assemble() the host verb uses, then builds the base image (hatago baked into harnessed-base, no separate hatago image), the derived per-stack image harnessed-<harness>-<stack>, and the fingerprint-gated per-stack volumes (tools:/install: at runtime, not as layers), merges installer-written settings back into the profile, and scans; a bare `harnessed build` reconciles every declared/previously-built (stack, harness) pair against the harnessed.recipe-hash image label.

host-run's accepted harnesses are exactly the rows of launcher._HOST_HARNESSES — claude (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) and omp (PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR) — the harnesses exposing an env var whose value IS a per-stack config/agent dir; a harness is absent because that row is unestablished, not because host mode is claude-shaped, and the record turns adding a harness into filling in a row rather than threading a second if harness == through the call sites.

The hatago MCP hub runs in-process inside the agent container, baked into harnessed-base — there is no separate hatago image — listening on a single Streamable-HTTP endpoint (default port 3535, HATAGO_PORT overridable), and the harness .mcp.json points only at that endpoint (or omits the hub when every declared server is direct).

harnessed test <stack> <harness>, exposed on both CLIs, is the integration oracle: it launches the stack --fresh headless and diffs the manifest-derived expectation (schema.expected_capabilities plus recipes' expect: blocks) against the live instance; its pure manifest-to-expected half takes no podman, which is what makes it unit-testable.

The --recipe surface composes a stack at launch time by minting a real stack.yaml under the generated catalog root, named from the CONTENT of the recipe set so the same set resolves to the same stack in every repo — one image, one pair of volumes — and so staleness, harnessed list, and both garbage collectors treat it like any other stack.

The Agent of Empires bridge (aoe.py) is optional, one-way, and register-only: it mirrors a launch into aoe's dashboard only after the backend's last validation gate, never drives harnessed, and every path in it degrades to silence — aoe absent, broken, or slow must never fail a launch, and HARNESSED_NO_AOE=1 disables it.

Beyond the five-group orientation map, the domain layer holds one module per concern — hosthome/hostrun (per-stack host home, host-mode installs/setups/inits), mounts/volumes/credmounts (mount set, per-stack volumes, credential forwarding), svcstate/svcguards (derived service identity plus destructive-start guards), launchenv/setupenv (launch-secret resolution and the folder-env contract), attachcmd (per-harness attach command and start-dir resolution), jsonmerge (the recursive settings merge), toollock (per-recipe mise.lock merging), dynstack, launchscript, persist (default-deny gate), persist_gc, capability/report/scan, prose (on-demand prose lint, never a build gate), catalogseed, aoe, and update.

host-run exists as its own Typer command rather than a mode of container-run because, beyond the shared stack-selection grammar, the two share only --rm and --fresh (and --fresh is shared spelling with different behavior: pod teardown on the container verb versus discarding the host build stamp and tool tree, #452), while --no-firewall, --no-secrets, --reauth, --shell, --mount-folder and --agent-start-folder all describe a pod that does not exist on a host launch, so a combined verb could only accept them and do nothing.

On the container backend the single container `run` is both the isolation boundary and the only way mounts and env cross it, and its env assembly relies on ORDER IS PRECEDENCE: the runtime applies -e left-to-right so the last wins, which is why catalog-authored recipe env: goes FIRST (it must not clobber harnessed-owned values) and harnessed-owned values come after — mirroring host mode, where _launch_host applies the recipe env to os.environ and then overwrites with harnessed-owned values; reversing the order on one path silently inverts precedence between the two modes.

harnessed-tools `test` is NOT runtime-free: it launches the stack --fresh headless and introspects the live pod, so it needs podman/docker just like `harnessed test`; only `assemble`, `persist-list`, `persist-prune` and `lint-prose` on that CLI are emit-only/host-only.

broker.py is the host secrets broker (epic #388 Topology B): one `varlock proxy` per container instance, spawned (not daemonized) on the host's loopback — where 1Password, the keychain, gpg-agent and a YubiKey can actually authenticate — started by the container launch only when the composed schema opts in with a @proxy annotation and --no-secrets was not passed (a failed start is fatal), recorded as a five-field state file under $XDG_STATE_HOME/harnessed/brokers that leaks no secret by construction, stopped with the pod, and reaped by reconcile() when a teardown never ran.

broker.py is an extracted module in the module map: it reports through the shared console, is imported by launcher.py (_broker_start_for / _broker_stop_for / _broker_report), is listed in tests/test_module_boundaries.py EXTRACTED with the note that it never lived in launcher.py — and it imports only paths and console, never launcher.

paths.BROKER_HOST_DOOR ("169.254.1.1") is a shared literal that three places must agree on for a pod to reach a varlock broker bound to the host's 127.0.0.1: paths.py defines it, the pod create's pasta --map-host-loopback option (mounts._mcp_remote_pod_args/_mcp_remote_pasta_net_args with broker=True) maps it into the pod, and the egress firewall ACCEPTs it (catalog/base/egress-firewall.sh) — which is why the constant lives in paths.py rather than in any one of the three (epic #388 Topology B; #436, #437).

The container create path runs in a fixed order with the secrets-broker slot in the middle: env resolution first (ContainerBackend.seed_auth calls launchenv._resolve_launch_secrets for the ordered global-then-project --env-file list, plus generated temps unlinked the moment the runtime ingests them), then the broker gate _broker_start_for inside apply_isolation(BOUNDARY) and immediately BEFORE pod create — the pod's --network args depend on whether a broker exists, so without one the pod gets no pasta --map-host-loopback route (a pod-less runtime starts no broker at all and creates a flat container) — then pod create, the single run that delivers mounts and env, setup scripts while egress is open, the egress close, and finally attach (os.execvp into runtime exec -it). A failed broker start aborts the launch, and if pod create then fails the already-started broker is stopped before the error re-raises.

The host launch path stops at env resolution and never touches the broker: _launch_host resolves the same global-then-project secret sources through launchenv._resolve_launch_env — a KEY->value map applied straight to os.environ in-process, never written to disk — then materializes, seeds auth, provisions and execs the harness directly; there is no broker gate, no pod create, and no attach, because a host launch resolves varlock natively with no boundary for a broker to sit on. tests/test_launch_parity.py's CONTAINER_ONLY ledger records _broker_start_for ('starts a host broker for a POD; a host launch resolves varlock natively'), proxy_schema_dirs, and _broker_stop_for as container-only by nature.

The supply-chain scan is a post-build stage owned by the launcher, not a Dockerfile layer: write_derived_dockerfile emits no scan layer (removed in bd harnessed-8px.21.5 — the layer scanned an image that no longer contained stack content and reported green off one scanner in four), and after the per-stack volumes are populated, `harnessed build` re-scans the just-built derived image credentialed (snyk + socket with tokens resolved host-side, volumes mounted so the scan sees what was installed); it is advisory — it reports posture and never fails the build, and --no-security-scans / HARNESSED_NO_SCANS skip it.

The broker gate's input is deliberately cheap: launchenv.proxy_schema_dirs returns the composed schema dirs (user-global ~/.config/harnessed, then the project) that opt in via a @proxy annotation form, decided by a text test on .env.schema that costs two file reads and NO varlock subprocess (proxy rules resolves values and can sit on a 1Password unlock prompt, so a launch that opted into nothing must not buy one); it mirrors _resolve_launch_secrets' dir selection so the broker resolves the same composed set the --env-file path resolves, and varlock absent from PATH means no broker and no error.

Pod launching belongs to the container backend alone: pod create, the member run, the attach, and every mount helper are container-backend stages, while HostBackend declares isolation=none, never creates a pod or container, and calls apply_isolation as a no-op in both phases precisely so the host path exercises the whole six-capability contract rather than quietly implementing five sixths of it.

The container backend's placement is runtime-parameterized, not podman-wired: paths.active_runtime() is the single runtime detector (ctrquery._runtime and everything downstream delegate to it), podman pods get USERNS_ARG (keep-id pinned to the image's uid/gid 1000, so the container's uid-1000 process IS the invoking user whatever their host uid) while docker gets DOCKER_USERNS_ARG (--userns=host) plus an explicit --user <invoking-uid>:0 whose value container_owner_ids couples to the volume chown so the two cannot drift; a rootless or unreadable docker daemon is refused before anything is created (docker_is_rootless returning None means refuse, never guess, and _preflight_runtime enforces it at the top of every launch), and a runtime that does not use pods creates a flat, self-owned-netns container and starts no secrets broker because there is no pasta door to deliver one through.

Each run verb is registered twice under #450: `host-exec` and `container-exec` are the SAME Typer functions as host-run/container-run (never forwarding wrappers), with ctx.info_name telling the body which verb was typed; a -exec invocation declares nobody-at-the-keyboard through console.set_exec_mode, and _can_prompt (a real TTY AND not exec mode) routes those launches down the non-interactive branch every caller already had, while the container attach drops -t so output is not drawn on an alternate screen buffer.

A global service's client address is resolved per launch mode, never baked: svcstate.svc_client_env fills the service's client_env `{host}` template with 127.0.0.1 for a host-mode agent and host.containers.internal for a containerized agent — both meaning the same host-published port — which is why the assembler emits hatago URL-proxy entries at host.containers.internal for containers while a host-run client dials loopback.
